title: rubus carpinifolius subsp. montanus
intro: Rubus carpinifolius subsp. montanus, commonly known as the Alpine Bramble, is a subspecies of flowering plant in the rose family. It is used in traditional medicine due to its health benefits, which include anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties that may help to lower cholesterol levels, reduce blood pressure, and prevent certain types of cancer. The therapeutic actions of this plant include analgesic, anti-diarrheal, and anti-ulcerative effects, which are attributed to its bioactive constituents, such as flavonoids, phenolic acids, and saponins. The bioactive constituents of Rubus carpinifolius subsp. montanus have been shown to exhibit antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and antimicrobial activities, which contribute to its therapeutic potential.
